title: NBA2 — questions that must be answered before a decision is reasonable
source_note: Each row is a decision, not a curiosity: it says what we already have, what is missing, how to close it, and what changes in the model once it is answered. Anything I could resolve from an official source this session was resolved instead of asked. 2026-11-14 (arena/6c5195d1-nba2): Q-23…Q-27 from the cross-check queue fragment analysis/queue-additions-5b80b88a.json are merged in (severity labels normalised to this register's vocabulary).

questions.question: Which odds source are we measuring against — and are we allowed to store its closing prices?
questions.have: The full slate, our lines, and the knowledge that NBA.com renders odds client-side only and picks.nba.com publishes none.
questions.missing: Any licensed book price, opening or closing, for any sport.
questions.how: Owner picks a vendor (theScore Sportsdata/Odds API, Sportradar, or a sportsbook affiliate feed) and confirms storage rights; then add an ingest to data/raw.
questions.impact: Everything. Without it there is no 'edge', no CLV, no gate G-02, no stake sizing, and no reason to prefer our number over a coin flip.

questions.question: Is the product a line-setting desk or a betting-picks desk?
questions.have: Both capabilities sketched: pricing engine (works) and bet selection with triggers (needs prices).
questions.missing: Owner decision on primary objective.
questions.how: Answer in one sentence; it changes which gate blocks promotion.
questions.impact: A line-setting desk is graded on MAE/calibration and is buildable today with zero market data. A picks desk is not buildable until Q-01 is resolved.

questions.question: What is the bankroll unit and the maximum stake per bet?
questions.have: A config default of 1% hard cap and quarter-Kelly.
questions.missing: Whether that is your risk tolerance at all.
questions.how: Owner states units (e.g. 1 unit = 0.25% of bankroll).
questions.impact: Kelly fraction, promotion criteria (G-09) and the reward pool's meaning.

questions.question: Do we accept that game-day injury data arrives too late for a T-3 publication?
questions.have: The official report's structure and cadence, plus proof: in the 11/13 16:15 ET release, all ten Nov 14 teams were 'NOT YET SUBMITTED'.
questions.missing: Whether you want T-3 lines (injury-blind) only, or a T-0 re-issue after the 13:00 ET report.
questions.how: Owner decision; implement as a second daily build at 13:30 ET.
questions.impact: Determines whether '3 days in advance' is a feature or a self-inflicted handicap. Our lines currently apply no injury adjustment at all.

questions.question: Can we get official player-level data (minutes, usage, on/off) from the build environment?
questions.have: The knowledge that stats.nba.com endpoints are unreachable from here and nba.com/stats tables are client-rendered.
questions.missing: An accessible official source or a licensed alternative.
questions.how: Test from the CI runner (different network than this sandbox); if still blocked, evaluate a commercial feed.
questions.impact: Props, prop combos, injury impact, and the margin/total correlation all sit behind this one answer.

questions.question: Do Emirates NBA Cup group games belong in the same distribution as ordinary regular-season games?
questions.have: The 11/13 slate is entirely Cup group play, and Cup games count for group standing with different incentives (winning by margin matters as a tiebreaker).
questions.missing: Historical evidence on whether Cup games differ in pace, rotations or margin distribution.
questions.how: Split the results snapshot by game_type once R-103 lands and test pace/margin differences.
questions.impact: If Cup games differ, today's entire slate is mis-calibrated and the model needs a game-type effect or an exclusion rule.

questions.question: Who ratifies the eleven unratified thresholds (disagreement tolerance, conviction cut, trigger hurdle, status→P(plays) weights, gate thresholds, ρ band)?
questions.have: Every one of them written down with its rationale and band on the Parameters page.
questions.missing: A decision, because they currently control which games are actionable.
questions.how: Owner reviews the Parameters page and either accepts or edits config.py.
questions.impact: Gate G-08 and Tier assignment are meaningless while thresholds are 'mine' rather than 'ours'.

questions.question: Is a 12-game sample enough to trade at all?
questions.have: Reliability weights ~0.74-0.78 and a fitted RMSE of 1.31 wins vs 2.78 baseline.
questions.missing: Your risk policy for early-season modelling.
questions.how: Owner decision; a hard rule could be 'no Tier A before 25 games'.
questions.impact: Decides whether this slate should have produced zero picks rather than 31 lines.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'removing luck' you will accept as a gate?
questions.have: Four candidate mechanisms implemented: bootstrap CI on PnL, t-stat ≥ 2, calibration slope, and rewards weighted on CLV/accuracy rather than PnL.
questions.missing: Whether you also require a variance-reduction metric (e.g. Sharpe of residualised PnL) or a holdout-only payout.
questions.how: Owner picks; add to gates.
questions.impact: Changes which strategies can win the leaderboard, and therefore what gets built next.

questions.question: How do you want the leaderboard to treat strategies that bet different numbers of games?
questions.have: Score components are per-bet averages, so abstention is neither rewarded nor punished beyond sample-size gates.
questions.missing: Whether volume should carry weight (e.g. minimum coverage per slate).
questions.how: Owner decision.
questions.impact: A 'bet three games a season' strategy can look elite without a volume term.

questions.question: Do we price parlays off our own singles only, or off book parlay prices when available?
questions.have: Correlation-swept joint pricing on our own numbers; the ratio (not the level) is publishable today.
questions.missing: Book parlay prices to compare against.
questions.how: Comes free with Q-01.
questions.impact: Determines whether S-04 is a strategy or an illustration.

questions.question: What is the correct treatment of a two-way/G-League assignment listed on the injury report?
questions.have: The report distinguishes 'G League - Two-Way', 'G League - On Assignment' and 'League Suspension' from injuries, and I count them as absent bodies.
questions.missing: Whether those absences should affect a rotation-floor model identically to injury.
questions.how: Owner decision; implement as a reason-class weighting in injuries.py.
questions.impact: Our rotation index currently treats a suspended starter and a assigned two-way as similar 'missing bodies' at different weights.

questions.question: Should rewards be paid at all before a strategy is promoted?
questions.have: Allocation logic that pays nothing when nothing is promoted (pool 100% unallocated).
questions.missing: Confirmation that you do not want an activity-based payout.
questions.how: Owner decision.
questions.impact: Paying for participation re-creates the exact incentive this project exists to remove.

questions.question: How should the site behave when the snapshot is stale?
questions.have: as-of and generated-at stamps on every page, and the build refuses to run on a future-dated slate.
questions.missing: A maximum-age policy (e.g. refuse to publish lines older than 24h).
questions.how: Add to lint + a scheduled build.
questions.impact: A 3-day-old line published as 'picks' is worse than no page.

questions.question: What is the procedure when a game is postponed or a star is ruled out at warmups?
questions.have: Nothing — the model has no re-quote path.
questions.missing: Trigger for re-pricing and a rule for voiding sealed predictions.
questions.how: Design a re-seal event in the ledger (new seal with reason, original kept).
questions.impact: Settling against a cancelled game would corrupt the leaderboard.

questions.question: Which team is 'home' when the schedule says an arena hosts a neutral-site or international game?
questions.have: None in this window; the schedule page marks neutralSite only in the JSON endpoints we cannot reach.
questions.missing: A rule + a data field.
questions.how: Add a `neutral` flag to the slate ingest, sourced from the game page.
questions.impact: HCA would be wrongly applied and every line for that game shifts ~1.5-3 points.

questions.question: Do we keep publishing from the repository root, or move to /docs?
questions.have: One workflow, root publish, working today.
questions.missing: Preference.
questions.how: Owner picks; /docs is a one-line workflow change.
questions.impact: Affects every relative link and the existing live URLs.

questions.question: Are we allowed to commit third-party ratings data (Basketball-Reference) into this public repo?
questions.have: One small facts table, each value linked to its source page, and Sports Reference's site terms are not re-checked here.
questions.missing: A licence/permission reading, or replacement with our own ingestion of official data.
questions.how: Owner/legal reads the source's terms of use; or implement R-104 and delete the file.
questions.impact: It is the only input to every line on the site today; if it must go, the model goes blind until R-104 lands.

questions.question: How many strategies is it honest to evaluate at once?
questions.have: 9 registered; G-06 deflation grows with the trial count.
questions.missing: A cap or a preregistration rule for new strategies.
questions.how: Add a trial registry (S-11) and require preregistration before evaluation.
questions.impact: With unlimited tries someone always wins the leaderboard by noise.

questions.question: Is the ledger's git-commit seal enough, or do you want an external timestamp?
questions.have: sha256 of canonical JSON, committed with the site.
questions.missing: Whether you need a trusted third-party timestamp (e.g. RFC3161) for the competition to be credible.
questions.how: Owner decides; if yes, add a timestamping step to the build.
questions.impact: Determines whether another session could dispute a seal after a bad run.

questions.question: What exactly should the executive summary optimise for — opportunity, risk, or project state?
questions.have: It currently reports project state and blockers first, because that is the truth today.
questions.missing: Whether you want a picks-first summary as soon as prices exist.
questions.how: Owner decision; the summary is generated, so it is a template change.
questions.impact: Avoids a summary that reads like a status report when you wanted a betting card.

questions.question: Which numbers on this site would change your decision if they moved by 10%?
questions.have: A sensitivity band for every structural parameter, and a stability fraction per line.
questions.missing: Your decision threshold — currently the model assumes ±10% matters, and suppresses a pick when it does.
questions.how: Owner states a threshold; encode in G-08.
questions.impact: This is the difference between a research dashboard and a betting system.

questions.question: Which execution environment can reach the official NBA endpoints, and under what policy?
questions.have: A dated, reproducible measurement from the sandbox: four endpoints, none answering at TLS. Plus the same result from three prior sessions. The `nba-ingest.yml` probe measures it from a GitHub-hosted runner and prints the table.
questions.missing: The runner's answer (recorded by the probe run), and the owner's decision about whether automated fetching of nba.com properties is in policy for this project at any cadence.
questions.how: Dispatch the probe from main; read the run summary; if reachable, confirm terms of use before enabling a schedule; if unreachable, mark ingestion 'blocked by source policy' in the requirements register instead of 'not started'.
questions.impact: Decides whether the daily-refresh requirement is an engineering task, a licensing task, or a manual one. Nothing downstream (CLV, settled ledger, promoted strategies) can start without it.

questions.question: Is the 13:00 ET referee PDF the authority for availability, and do we keep the bytes?
questions.have: Three different stamps of the same day's report are cited across surfaces (01:00 PM, 04:15 PM, 05:15 PM ET) and the reconciliation table already adjudicates 10 status changes between them. The capture tool archives the PDF with a sha256 of the response body.
questions.missing: A policy: which stamp is canonical for a published line, and whether archived PDFs (or only their hashes) are kept in-repo.
questions.how: Owner picks 'latest release before tip, with the previous two retained'; then the ingest stores the PDF, its hash, and its stamp with every snapshot.
questions.impact: Without a canonical stamp, two honest sessions will keep disagreeing about who is Out, and the disagreement will look like a model difference.

questions.question: Which surface is canonical, and what happens to the other four?
questions.have: Six published surfaces now: the root generated site (36 tables / 964 rows), `docs/`, `dashboard/`, `originated/`, `verified/`, and `backtest/**` added by PR #28 with its own engine, report JSON, pages and verifier. Each has a passing checker for itself; none is subordinate to another.
questions.missing: An owner decision: which surface is canonical, whether backtest/** is integrated into data/site.json or kept as an annex, and a rule for what a new session may write into — because a session that wants to publish measured results currently has no option except a new tree.
questions.how: Pick one; move the others to `archive/` with a redirect note on each landing, or keep them and put the surface inventory (already a published table) at the top of the landing page.
questions.impact: Five surfaces means five answers to 'what is our line for DEN@NOP', all defensible, none canonical. That is the failure mode a leaderboard project cannot afford.

questions.question: What does a strategy have to survive before it can be paid?
questions.have: Nine gates per strategy defined and applied to 9 strategies (90 gate results, all BLOCKED/AT-RISK); a pre-registered sealed ledger (22 predictions, digest on every page); a tier ladder with reward weights; and a stated minimum sample of 300 settled bets.
questions.missing: Owner sign-off on the promotion rule as a *policy*, not a design: minimum sample, holdout window, vig treatment, drawdown cap, multiple-comparison correction across nine strategies, and what happens to the seal when the window rolls forward daily.
questions.how: Write it into the requirements register as acceptance criteria, then let the gate code enforce it; anything not enforced is a poster.
questions.impact: Until this exists, 'top performing strategies' has no definition, so the competition cannot start — and the honest answer today is that the leaderboard is empty by design.

questions.question: Who reviews a commit that the nightly ingest pushes to `main`?
questions.have: `refresh.yml` runs with `contents: write`, rebuilds the site, and pushes `HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` directly, gated by its own verify chain (unit tests, seal verification, provenance lint) and an explicit guard that the sealed ledger is untouched. That is a sound fail-closed design for a bot.
questions.missing: A stated policy on what a bot commit may change on `main` without a human: the pipeline today also carries F1's negative-count bug, which such a commit would happily re-publish with a green tick.
questions.how: Add the cross-check to the ingest verify chain (S-21/S-30) so a bot cannot push a build that fails semantic review, and record the bot's allowed paths in the requirements register.
questions.impact: Determines whether automated refresh is trustworthy end-to-end. Right now it can only fail loudly, not fail subtly — which is good — but 'loudly' is scoped to what CI checks today.
